description: A two-panel SEM micrograph set (secondary-electron, cross-section) of Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steel after the 750 °C intermediate heat treatment of the MHT process. (a) Low-magnification view with a 10 µm scale bar at bottom right: largely equiaxed grains separated by dark, irregularly thickened, in places discontinuous grain boundaries; a few rounded dark particles sit inside grains; a white dashed rectangle in the centre marks the region enlarged in (b). (b) Higher-magnification view with a 2 µm scale bar at bottom right: the boundary network resolves into chains of closely spaced bright/light precipitates forming nodular, discontinuous films along the grain boundaries, one boundary triple junction is clearly imaged, and a grain interior shows faint parallel straight lines (twin lamellae) plus a few small bright particles. Together the panels establish that the 750 °C intermediate heat treatment leaves a dense, closely spaced grain-boundary precipitate population decorating the boundaries of the MHT specimen — the feature the citing text links to increased stress in non-twinned regions, more twin nucleation sites and more special boundaries that interfere with RHAGBs. Only the two scale bars are printed; no numeric data labels appear.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a SEM micrograph whose scale bar reads 10 µm, located bottom right.
Panel (a) shows equiaxed grains separated by dark, irregularly thickened and locally discontinuous grain boundaries, with a few rounded dark particles inside grains.
A white dashed rectangle is drawn in the centre of panel (a), marking the region reproduced at higher magnification in panel (b).
Panel (b) carries a 2 µm scale bar bottom right, i.e. it is at higher magnification than panel (a) with its 10 µm scale bar.
In panel (b) the grain boundaries appear as closely spaced, bright/light nodular precipitates forming discontinuous films along the boundaries, and a boundary triple junction is clearly visible.
Panel (b) shows faint parallel straight lines within a grain interior, consistent with twin lamellae, alongside a small number of tiny bright particles.
The caption states that (a) is a cross-section of a sample subjected to intermediate heat treatment at 750 °C in the MHT process and that (b) shows the localized region of (a) at 'low magnification'.
The caption's description of (b) as 'low magnification' conflicts with the 2 µm scale bar visible in (b), which indicates a higher magnification than the 10 µm bar in (a).

The citing text asserts that the 750 °C intermediate heat treatment applied to the MHT specimens resulted in the distribution of many precipitates at the grain boundaries, as shown in Fig. 9(a and b).

The citing text states that these closely spaced precipitates increased stress in the non-twinned regions, producing a larger number of twin nucleation sites and finally more special boundaries that interfered with the RHAGBs.

The citing text reports special-boundary percentages of 71.7 %, 68.3 % and 71.2 % for the three specimens, increasing for the S1050 and multi-stage heat treatment conditions; these values are not printed on either micrograph.
The caption identifies the imaged material condition only as the MHT sample given 750 °C intermediate heat treatment; no alloy composition is printed on the panels themselves.

subfigures.description: Low-magnification SEM micrograph of the cross-sectioned MHT specimen after 750 °C intermediate heat treatment; 10 µm scale bar bottom right. Equiaxed grains bounded by dark, irregularly thickened and locally discontinuous grain boundaries, scattered rounded dark intra-granular particles, and a central white dashed rectangle marking the region shown in (b).

Higher-magnification SEM micrograph of the dashed localized region of (a); 2 µm scale bar bottom right. Grain boundaries are resolved as chains of closely spaced bright/light precipitates forming nodular discontinuous films; a boundary triple junction and a grain interior with faint parallel twin-lamella lines are visible. The caption calls this panel 'low magnification', which does not match the smaller 2 µm scale bar (i.e. higher magnification) seen in the pixels.

unreadable_items: Panel (b) is labelled 'low magnification' in the caption but shows a 2 µm scale bar (higher magnification than the 10 µm bar in (a)) — caption/pixel disagreement
No composition, grain-size value or precipitate-size value is printed on either panel
